clue.text: Backchat evincing spite or otherwise?

indicators.note: otherwise asks for the letters of spite and or to be arranged differently

explanation.surface: A question of whether a cheeky reply shows malice or something else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'otherwise' rearranges SPITE OR into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick sharp retort is backchat, a witty reply thrown back at someone.

clue.text: This is beneath 22,which is rare

parts.note: beneath means under
the answer to 22, spent, means finished or done

explanation.surface: A cross-reference that makes the reader look up another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 22 is SPENT, here in its sense of used up, finished, giving DONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat cooked only lightly is called rare.

clue.text: Strong liquor gives a tingle, nothing more

indicators.note: more says the next piece is added on

parts.note: a sting is a sharp tingle
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: Hard spirits produce a warm tingle and do nothing else.
explanation.walkthrough: STINGO is an old word for strong ale or beer.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic name for potent beer, which is a strong alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Having regard to programme for resort

parts.note: re means concerning, with regard to
a course is a programme of study or treatment

explanation.surface: Considering a schedule of events at a holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place but is the noun meaning something turned to for help.
explanation.definitionFit: Having recourse to something means turning to it as a last resort or fallback.

clue.text: Rips aren't seen to make complaints

indicators.note: make signals that the preceding letters are formed into something new

explanation.surface: Tears that go unnoticed lead to grievances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make' rearranges the letters of RIPS AREN'T SEEN TO into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal representations are protests or objections lodged with an authority.

clue.text: Note the residue only is material

parts.note: C is a musical note
ash is the residue left after burning
mere means only, nothing more than

explanation.surface: A remark that only leftovers count as substance.
explanation.definitionFit: This soft fine wool from Kashmir goats is a fabric.

clue.text: Both articulate and thorough

definitions.meaning: to articulate is to say or voice

explanation.definitionFit: To utter is to speak; as an adjective it means total or complete.

clue.text: Hoarding gold in smart environment

indicators.note: environment says the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: to smart is to sting
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Precious metal kept somewhere stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoarding means putting things away and keeping them in reserve.

clue.text: Flighty creature with money in bag

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound, money
to net is to bag or catch

explanation.surface: A capricious person carrying cash in a sack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flighty' suggests fickle, but means able to fly: a small songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: A small finch, so a bird, a creature of flight.

clue.text: Getting around ten points possibly just for standing

indicators.note: getting around says one piece encloses the other
possibly suggests the letters of points may be rearranged

parts.note: ten written as the figures 1 and 0 looks like IO

explanation.surface: A scoring system that gives about ten points for merely standing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ten' is the number 10 drawn as letters; 'possibly' scrambles the points and 'Getting around' wraps them round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's standing is their rank or status.

clue.text: A man of some authority in time taking over normally

indicators.note: in says the answer lies within the words that follow

explanation.surface: An official who will eventually take charge as a matter of course.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs through takinG OVER NORmally.
explanation.definitionFit: A governor heads a colony, prison or state, wielding power.

clue.text: He'll bring many craft in

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, many
art means craft or skill

explanation.surface: A captain who will sail a large fleet into port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'craft' suggests boats but means skill; Martin is simply a man's name, the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A common forename for a man, so a he.

clue.text: Academic bosses must admit financial liability

indicators.note: must admit says one piece goes inside another

parts.note: bosses are studs, raised knobs
an IOU is a written note of debt

explanation.surface: Senior managers have to own up to a debt.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookish, scholarly person is academic.

clue.text: They are dependent on hearing devices

definitions.text: They are dependent on hearing devices

parts.words: They are dependent on hearing devices
parts.note: dependent means hanging from, and the hearing devices are ears: jewellery that dangles from them

explanation.definitionFit: Ornaments worn hanging from the lobes of the ears.

clue.text: Extreme, even in its amended version

indicators.note: an amended version changes the order of the letters of even in its

explanation.surface: A severe rule, even after it has been revised.
explanation.definitionFit: Intensive care or farming is concentrated and highly forceful.

clue.text: The underworld have the answer — vanish!

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld and its name
to answer a puzzle is to solve it

explanation.surface: The dead know the secret and then disappear.
explanation.definitionFit: To fade away and melt into nothing.

clue.text: Stealing off to see an old fashioned doctor

indicators.note: off indicates that the letters of stealing are disordered

explanation.surface: A thief slipping away to visit a traditional physician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges STEALING. Galen was the ancient Greek physician whose followers practised outdated medicine.
explanation.definitionFit: A follower of the ancient Greek physician Galen, an outmoded medical practitioner.

clue.text: State date of birth as usual

parts.note: aver means state or declare
your date of birth tells your age

explanation.surface: Giving one's birthday as a matter of routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Average means typical, ordinary.

clue.text: Clement the Marxist could appear congenial

parts.note: clement means mild or kind
a red is a communist or Marxist

explanation.surface: A man called Clement, a communist, may seem friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clement' looks like a name but is the adjective meaning merciful.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindred spirits are like-minded, having similar natures.

clue.text: A sweet drink (soft) that is offered around very quietly

indicators.note: offered around says the drink encloses the next piece

parts.note: ale is a drink
pp is pianissimo, very quiet in music
p is piano, soft in music
ie is id est, that is

explanation.surface: A soft drink served with a dessert and passed round in hushed tones.
explanation.definitionFit: A baked dessert of fruit in pastry is a pudding.

clue.text: Meet and stay with royal characters

parts.note: a prop is a stay or support
ER are the royal initials Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Gather together and lodge with the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Meet' looks like a verb but is the old adjective meaning fitting.
explanation.definitionFit: Meet as an adjective means suitable or appropriate.

clue.text: The people count-that's official!

parts.note: read as a headcount of the whole population carried out by government

explanation.definitionFit: An official enumeration of the population.

clue.text: A writer found lying in the street more dead than alive

indicators.note: found lying in says one piece sits inside another

parts.note: St is short for street
a pen is a writing implement

explanation.surface: An author discovered collapsed in the road, barely living.
explanation.definitionFit: Exhausted, worn out, used up.

clue.text: King Edmund's press team

parts.note: to iron is to press clothes
a side is a team

explanation.surface: The media relations staff of a medieval king.
explanation.walkthrough: Edmund II of England was nicknamed Ironside.
explanation.definitionFit: The byname of the eleventh-century English king Edmund II.

clue.text: Involved later in court battle

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the other piece

parts.note: to court is to woo

indicators.note: involved suggests the letters of later are tangled

explanation.surface: Later on, caught up in a legal fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'court' looks legal but is the verb of wooing; 'Involved' scrambles the later letters, and 'in' puts them inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1815 clash where Napoleon was defeated.

clue.text: Wanted to finish without challenge

parts.note: end means finish
to vie is to compete or challenge

explanation.surface: Hoped to end things without opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense of outside, as in the hymn's 'a green hill far away, without a city wall'.
explanation.definitionFit: Envied means coveted, desired what another has.

clue.text: Not supported, so unsettled

definitions.meaning: having no rest, a support or prop

explanation.definitionFit: Restless means fidgety, unable to relax; split, it means lacking a support.
